beats: [d:tension][act:grave, steady]In {1932|nineteen thirty-two}, government doctors began to ^watch ^six hundred Black men in ^Alabama. [act:quiet, precise]Three hundred and ^ninety-nine of them had ^syphilis: a serious infection that, untreated, can harm the heart and the ^brain over years. [act:measured, explaining]The other two hundred and one, without it, were there for ^comparison.
[d:tension][act:low, letting it sit]They were ^never ^told what they had.

[d:calm][p:0.93][act:quiet, placing us there]Macon County, ^Alabama, in the American South. [act:measured, the deception]The men were told they were being ^treated for 'bad blood', a vague local phrase for many ^ailments. [act:plainly, heavy]They were given hot ^meals, ^rides, and money for their ^burials.
[d:build][act:cold, deliberate]The real aim: to watch what ^untreated syphilis does@verb to the human body, all the way to ^autopsy, the medical examination after ^death.

[d:build][p:0.93][act:plain fact, even]By {1943|nineteen forty-three}, the antibiotic ^penicillin had become the standard ^cure for syphilis. [act:slower, heavy]The men were ^not offered it. [sfx:hit][go:3|0][act:steady, holding back]The study kept ^going. [act:the weight of it, slow]For ^twenty-nine more years. [p:0.9][act:quiet, letting it land]Almost a whole ^generation.
[d:build][p:0.93][act:plain storytelling, respectful]In {1966|nineteen sixty-six}, Peter ^Buxtun, a government health investigator, ^objected. [act:dry, disappointed]He was ^brushed off.

[d:build][act:neutral, setting it up]In {1969|nineteen sixty-nine}, a government ^panel reviewed the study... [act:quiet disbelief, slower]and voted to ^continue. [gap:0.4][p:0.9][act:quiet, heavy]By then, the cure had existed for twenty-six ^years.

[d:reveal][act:resolve, picking up pace]So Buxtun went to the ^press. [act:clear, brisk]In July {1972|nineteen seventy-two}, Jean ^Heller, a reporter at the Associated Press news agency, broke the ^story. [act:quiet relief]Four months later, that November, the study ^ended.

[d:build][act:measured, sober]A legal ^settlement followed, for the men and their ^families. [p:0.93][act:solemn, with care]And in {1997|nineteen ninety-seven}, a presidential ^apology, from Bill ^Clinton. [p:0.9][act:quoting him, gently]'What was done cannot be ^undone. [act:continuing the quote, softly]But we can end the ^silence.'

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:grave, weighing it][tune:rise]Left untreated, on ^purpose, for decades? [act:firm, sober][tune:fall]^*Established*, by the government's ^own records@noun. [p:0.93][act:asking it, steady]How do we ^know? [act:clear, measured]From the ^paper trail: the study's own files, and an official panel's report in {1973|nineteen seventy-three}. [p:0.9][act:the everyday picture, grave]Papers written at the time, by those in charge: like a captain's own ^logbook, the strongest kind of ^evidence.

[d:tension][p:0.93][act:gentle, to the viewer]The ^rules changed: a new law in {1974|nineteen seventy-four}, review boards for research on people, and the Belmont Report in {1979|nineteen seventy-nine}. [act:warm, the last word]It's one big ^reason every medical study now has to ask for your ^consent, in ^writing.
